dispositions.reason: Approved AC-7 demands no copy of the old secret in process memory, which the plan itself says a unit test cannot show; only a SPEC amendment (e.g. 'the stored hash is cleared by a stated deadline') can resolve it, not a plan-level reinterpretation.

Pending the AC-7 decision, the plan must state the sweep-lag bound explicitly and add a test that drives startKeySweeper (injected clock and interval) rather than only calling sweepExpiredKeys directly.

Verified in src/store.js: each MIGRATIONS[n] step must return the document at version n+1, and migrate() loops on schemaVersion; the plan's MIGRATIONS[2] step must say it sets schemaVersion: 3 or loading an existing file never terminates.

Forward-only versioned migrations are the store's existing design (src/store.js header); rollback by restoring a pre-upgrade copy is a deploy concern outside the SPEC's scope and the build does not need it.

The plan must state the expiresAt representation (e.g. epoch milliseconds or ISO string parsed to ms on both sides of the comparison) in rotateKey, authenticate and sweepExpiredKeys, because JSON round-trips a Date to a string and a direct comparison never expires the key.
startKeySweeper needs declared error handling (catch around the transact call, so a failed write cannot become an unhandled rejection that kills the server) and a test for it.

AC-3/AC-4 require distinct key_expired/key_revoked answers, yet the plan clears the revoked hash and answers on the id alone; the plan must either state this as an explicit human-confirmed trade-off or verify the secret first for dead keys, and it must reconcile the src/auth.js same-401 comment. I cannot tell which, so it goes to re-plan and then the supervisor.

SPEC Intent says the old key keeps working during the grace so integrations can be redeployed; restricting deprecated principals would be new behaviour outside the SPEC's scope and would cut against that intent.
The SPEC asks for no logging or metrics and adding them would be speculative scope (P7); the sweeper-failure handling that matters for correctness is covered by the G1-6 replan.
Both orderings satisfy AC-6; omitting key.created is a plan choice already listed in the plan, and the SPEC's audit scope names only rotation and revocation entries, so the build needs no change.

SPEC Constraint 3 (404 on every key route) and AC-5 (member gets 403) overlap for a member targeting another org's key; the plan must list the admin-first-then-lookup order among the choices it flags for the human.
The plan must say whether error responses (403/404/409/422) to a deprecated key also carry Deprecation: true and how createApp's catch path gets the principal, so the build is not left to guess.
Add a test in test/keys-edge.test.js (or the AC-2 test) asserting that a non-deprecated key, including the newly issued one, gets no Deprecation header, so an unconditional header cannot pass.

To keep one change-reason per file (P3), move startKeySweeper and its interval lifecycle out of src/server.js into its own declared module, add it to the Files list and have the import.meta.main block call it. I cannot tell the file is fine as is.
